This standalone page exercises the interactive Matplotlib path provided by
`pyodide-interaktiv`. Render it from the repository root with:

```bash
quarto render plots_test.qmd
```

Each test cell contains its own imports and can be rerun independently. A plot
first appears as a PNG and is then replaced by WebAgg. Check that titles,
MathText, labels and legends remain complete; that the toolbar controls stay in
fixed positions while its status text changes; and that pan, zoom, reset and
download work.

## 1. Text, MathText and changing toolbar status

Move the pointer over the plot and every toolbar button. The coordinates and
helper text must appear on the fixed row below the controls without moving the
buttons.

```{pyodide-python}
#| label: webagg-line
#| autorun: true

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
ax.plot(x, np.sin(x), label=r"$\sin(x)$")
ax.plot(x, np.cos(x), label=r"$\cos(x)$")
ax.set_title(r"Two periodic functions: $y=\sin(x)$ and $y=\cos(x)$")
ax.set_xlabel(r"angle $x$ (radians)")
ax.set_ylabel("function value")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 2. Four images and subplot titles

This is the regression case that exposed the old canvas backend: titles and
other text were correct in the initial PNG but became incomplete after the
interactive canvas replaced it.

```{pyodide-python}
#| label: webagg-images
#| autorun: true

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

X1 = np.full((4, 4), 0.5)
X2 = np.array([
    [0.1, 0.9, 0.1, 0.9],
    [0.9, 0.1, 0.9, 0.1],
    [0.1, 0.9, 0.1, 0.9],
    [0.9, 0.1, 0.9, 0.1],
])
Y1 = X1.reshape(2, 2, 2, 2).mean(axis=(1, 3))
Y2 = X2.reshape(2, 2, 2, 2).mean(axis=(1, 3))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(8, 2.25))
for ax, image, title in zip(
    axes,
    [X1, X2, Y1, Y2],
    ["Input $X_1$", "Input $X_2$", "Output from $X_1$", "Output from $X_2$"],
):
    ax.imshow(image, cmap="gray", vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 3. Snap cursor on points and bars

Move the pointer near a scatter point and over a bar. The custom snap cursor
must still display the nearest values on top of WebAgg.

```{pyodide-python}
#| label: webagg-snap
#| autorun: true

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.25))

u = np.linspace(0, 1, 12)
ax1.scatter(u, u**2 + rng.normal(0, 0.025, len(u)), label="measurements")
ax1.plot(u, u**2, color="tab:orange", label=r"$u^2$")
ax1.set_title("Points and curve")
ax1.set_xlabel("input $u$")
ax1.legend()

names = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
values = [2, 5, 3, 4]
ax2.bar(names, values, color=["#8ecae6", "#ffcf70", "#a8d5a2", "#d7b5e8"])
ax2.set_title("Bars")
ax2.set_ylabel("value")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 4. Multiple figures from one cell

Both figures must remain visible and receive their own complete toolbar.

```{pyodide-python}
#| label: webagg-multiple
#| autorun: true

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

u = np.linspace(0, 1, 12)
for power in (2, 3):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 2.5))
    ax.plot(u, u**power)
    ax.set_title(rf"The power $u^{power}$")
    ax.set_xlabel("u")
    ax.set_ylabel(rf"$u^{power}$")
    plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 5. Explicit static fallback

`canvas: false` must keep this as a normal PNG without a WebAgg toolbar.

```{pyodide-python}
#| label: webagg-static
#| autorun: true
#| canvas: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 2.5))
ax.plot([0, 1, 2], [0, 1, 0], marker="o")
ax.set_title("Deliberately static PNG")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
